subject: Now, my primary residence could be “seized”
body: BREAKING: A federal judge is now considering… ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏  Dear Friend, On October 22, a federal judge decreed that I had 7days to hand over my home in New York – as well as my only car and sentimentalkeepsakes and heartfelt gifts that I collected over the span of 80 years. Ithought that would be the end of the damage… But with the election rightaround the corner, Kamala’s Deep State truly wants to ruin me with all they’vegot. They’re now considering dealing one final blow to me. A judge may noworder me to give up my remaining home in Florida – my primary residence. As mylawyer inquired: do they truly want me homeless? Over the last few days, we’veheard ridiculous claims about President Trump being a “fascist.” Let me tellyou what fascism is… Fascism is weaponizing the legal system to punish yourpolitical opponents. Fascism is having your home taken from you. Fascism istaking the law license away from your opponent’s lawyer. Fascism is trying toturn your enemies into political prisoners. I am living through theDemocrats’ fascism right now. I sincerely pray that freedom, justice, and thetruth prevail on Tuesday, November 5 – or the damage done to me will spreadlike wildfire to the rest of our great Republic. But, as I wrote to you in anearlier letter, the Bible reminds us that our earthly possessions will alwaysfade, but greater “heavenly treasures” await us. The pursuit of truth,freedom, and justice are worth infinitely more than a car or a home.Possessions come and go, but I couldNEVER SURRENDER my fight for freedom andfor what I know to betrue. I would be tone deaf if I didn’t acknowledge thattimes are tough right now for all Americans, not just me, so please stopreading here if you cannot give at this time. But funding my Legal DefenseTrust is my last remaining hope of fighting for my freedom and for the libertyand justice of all Americans. So, if you can, and, seriously, only if you can,please make a contribution to my Legal Defense Trust – the Rudy GiulianiFreedom Fund – as I keep fighting for my freedom and justice as Kamala’s DeepState tries to JAIL me for life. subject: I’ve spent a lot of time with Tim Kaine
body: Derek, I’ve had the honor of being Tim Kaine’s friend since we met at HarvardLaw School in 1980. For over 40 years, I’ve watched him wholeheartedly serveVirginia, first as mayor of Richmond, then as my Lieutenant Governor, andlater Governor, before serving together in the United States Senate. Thismeans I’ve spent a lot of time with Tim and gathered plenty of intel on him.So as I sat down to write this email asking you to support Senator Kaine’s re-election campaign, I found myself wondering exactly what I should say to youto assure you that Tim is the right choice to represent Virginia in Congress.And then it dawned on me: I want to tell you the top 3 things that annoy methe most about Tim Kaine. First off, Tim is way too nice! As a former civilrights attorney and missionary, he’s spent his entire career committed tosocial justice, being driven by the value of kindness and the belief that itcan change peoples’ lives. And he’s a genuinely good guy on top of that.Second, he’s ridiculously good at playing the harmonica. Seriously, he carriesthem in his briefcase, just in case a jam session breaks out on the Senatefloor. Third and finally, and I’ve said this before, he’s a deeply optimisticperson. Sometimes I can be a glass half-empty kind of guy, but Tim’s alwaysseems about ⅔ full. We need someone like Tim Kaine in the Senate. Tim’s valueof kindness and decency is what drives his undying dedication to serving thepeople of Virginia. And in a Congress plagued by partisan division, Tim’srelentless optimism keeps him from giving up in the crucial fights to protectvoting rights, safeguard a woman’s right to choose, and more. Now theharmonica… that one might not always translate to his work as a Senator, it’sjust really great to watch. The thing is, Tim’s seat could very well determineif the GOP takes control on Tuesday. Republicans are working overtime to ousthim and take back control of the Senate. body:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    [https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20241101-4478-footer&t;=1001&akid;=4478%2E420207%2EstGsbt]Pramila Jayapal Peter, This week, South Asians across the world arecelebrating Diwali, a festival that speaks to the deepest hopes of ourcommunity. Also known as the Festival of Lights, it’s a moment ofillumination, of connection, and of profound possibility. And this year, itjust so happens to coincide with an election in which we’ll have the chance toelect the first-ever South Asian as President of the United States. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/pj-email-20241101-2?refcode=em20241101-4478&refcode2;=4478_420207_stGsbt&akid;=4478%2E420207%2EstGsbt][IMG] On election night in 2016, Kamala Harris and I broke barriers together.I became the first South Asian woman ever elected to the House ofRepresentatives, and she became the first South Asian woman ever elected tothe Senate. Now we stand at the brink of an even more transformative moment.It’s not just a political milestone. It's a testament to the journey ofgenerations of people who have worked, dreamed, and persevered to get us tothis moment. Our community's story is one of resilience — of voices thatrefuse to be dimmed and of traditions that continue to shine brightly acrosscontinents. We see this in the vibrant celebrations happening in homes andcommunities across the nation. In the glow of clay lamps, in the warmth ofshared meals, in the sparkle of joy that connects us. To our diverse SouthAsian community — Hindus, Muslims, Sikhs, Christians, Jains — this is a momentto honor our collective strength. To recognize the challenges we face, thefears that sometimes shadow our experiences, and also the power we have touplift, to support, and to create meaningful change. As we gather with familyand friends, let us recommit ourselves to a future of true belonging. Whereevery voice matters, where every story is heard, where our collective lightcan transform our shared landscape. subject: I’ll tell you what I believe:
body: [1]Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress We live in a constant state ofinjustice. We are always struggling against systems of mass incarceration, ofextreme income inequality, of late stage capitalism. Those conditions doexist. But one thing that I think is important is that we must mobilize for anaffirmative vision for this country — we can’t just mobilize on fear. We needto be clear about what the stakes are. We do. But I don’t believe in a ‘fearonly’ approach. I’ll tell you what I believe: I believe in a bare minimum. $15minimum wage needed to be passed several years ago. I believe in guaranteed,improved, and expanded Medicare to every single American. We can’t give up.I’ve been in that place when I was a waitress. I did spend some time giving upand being cynical and saying, “F*ck this.” And you know what it got us?Nothing. Depression, cynicism, and a sense of purposelessness. Giving up is aprivilege that people just can’t afford. Movements wax and wane. And there aretimes when it feels like our power is waning, and it’s really easy to take ourball and go home. But the strength of a movement really depends on thedurability of it, and the commitment to it. That black pill of cynicism is thedeath of movements, not the birth of them.
